To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have established an HBV infection model using HepG2 NTPC cells that can be used for the development of antiviral drugs.
the HepG2 NTPC cells can be efficiently infected by clinical primary isolates of HBV, and that HBV ccc DNA could be detected in the infected cells.
we provide detailed protocols to efficiently infect HepG2 NTPC cells with HBV, and to study HBV infection in this cell line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a HepG2 NTPC cell line that can be used to study HBV infection and antivirals targeting HBV ccc DNA.
the development of a robust and reliable system to study HBV infection and replication in vitro.
the development of a novel cell culture system for HBV infection, which is expected to be a valuable tool for the study of HBV biology and the development of novel anti-HBV drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HepG2 NTPC cell line is a valuable tool for the study of HBV infection, but it should be used in conjunction with other cell culture systems to fully characterize the infection process and identify novel antiviruses.
the protocols described here can be readily adapted to other hepatoma cell lines and used as a model system to study HBV life cycle.
the protocols described here can be readily adapted to other cell types and viruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HBV can efficiently infect HepG2 NTcp cells, and the infection can be readily detected by immunostaining of viral antigens and Southern blots.
HepG2 NTPC cells are a useful and reliable tool for HBV research, and the protocols described here could serve as a reference for future HBV studies using this cell line.
HepG2 NTPC cells can serve as a valuable tool for the study of HBV infection, and for the development of novel anti-HBV agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the infection efficiency of HepG2 cells is greatly enhanced with the use of a single cell clone of HepG2-NTCP cells, and the infection efficiency of these cells can be further improved with the use of HBV inoculum produced from DNA-transfected HepG2 NTCD cells.
HepG2 NTPC cells are highly susceptible to infection with HBV and can be used for a variety of studies.
HBV infection of the HepG2 NTcp cell line is efficient and reproducible, and that the cell line can be used to identify and study HBV infection in vitro.
